column1: # The image-descriptor fixtures, and the verdict each one should earn.
# `cpp` is what app_image::validate() should answer; `python` is whether
# tools/app_image.py's check() should come back with no problems. Both are stated
# rather than derived, so a change in either implementation shows up here as a
# disagreement with what was intended rather than as two implementations quietly
# `n-a` means the case is not one that side can be asked. It is not a way to
# excuse a failure: every n-a carries a reason in its note.
# Tab-separated rather than JSON so both a Python test and a C++ one can read it in
# a few lines. A hand-rolled JSON parser in the suite would be more code to get
# wrong than the thing under test.
# Regenerate the images with: python test/fixtures/app_image/make_fixtures.py

column5: a sealed image, descriptor patched and trailer correct
no descriptor at 0x200: app_image.cpp unlinked or the vector table grew over it
the size field was never patched, so the sealing post-build step did not run
size is not word-aligned, and the build pads to 4 bytes before the trailer
size is smaller than a descriptor plus a trailer
size exceeds the app region this product reserves
sealed, then the trailer corrupted: what an aborted flash leaves behind

the declared size is honest and its CRC is right, but the file runs on past it. validate() judges a region of flash and reads only `size` bytes, so it is satisfied; check() judges a file and refuses a size that disagrees with the length on disk. A real difference in what the two are asked, not a divergence.

too small to hold a descriptor. validate() reads at HEADER_OFFSET before it knows any size, so a buffer shorter than that is a precondition it does not accept rather than a verdict it returns; the bootloader can never present one, because its region is always larger.
